title: Support scoping `autocomplete` suggestions to the sites domain
body:
Currently, [`autocomplete`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofilling-form-controls:-the-autocomplete-attribute) suggestions are shared across sites which works great for many of the spec'ed out detail tokens like `email`, address, credit card, etc. But this doesn't work well for a general input like search.

As a real world example, if you use `<input type="search" name="q">` in your own app, it will show a bunch of results from your GitHub issue and PR searches (because they also have an `input` with `name="q"`). If Google didn't have `autocomplete="off"` you would also see all of your Google searches. Or if you use `<input type="search" name="search">`, you will probably see results from searching your Amazon order history. These are just examples you would probably run into and be familiar with as a developer but the cross-contamination is unlimited.

Searches aren't very relevant cross-site most of the time. I don't expect to find relevant results using one my Amazon searches in my own app searching for Matrix rooms.

I was able to find one other conversation around this: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60838558/how-to-improve-browser-autocomplete-suggestions-without-turning-them-off

### Alternatives

#### Browsers could respect custom `autocomplete` values

Currently, if you try to use a custom `autocomplete` value, it seems to be ignored and the autocomplete results are solely based on the `name` attribute, ex. `<input type="search" autocomplete="matrix-public-archive-search">` (spawning from https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-public-archive/pull/70)

This was also mentioned in the Chrome tracker as a solution but Chrome and Firefox don't behave this way. They both ignore and have the normal shared suggestions based on the `name` attribute.

> As an example, if you have an address input field in your CRM tool that you don't want Chrome to Autofill, you can give it semantic meaning that makes sense relative to what you're asking for: e.g. autocomplete="new-user-street-address".  If Chrome encounters that, it won't try and autofill the field.
>
> *-- https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=468153#c164*


#### Support custom autocomplete suggestions/results

Add a way to supply and populate the `autocomplete` suggestions. Let the app can manage it's own suggestions.
